episode_title: Are Companies Wasting Money on Data & AI?

real_qa.q: What is FTE debt and how does it relate to hidden costs of data investments?
real_qa.r: FTE debt refers to the hidden cost of data where full-time employee time intended for business-value activities like generating campaigns or creating tickets gets diverted to data work that should be handled by the data team. This includes time spent pulling CSV files, quality checking data, verifying dashboard numbers against sources, and building additional dashboards when existing ones don't meet business needs.

real_qa.q: Why should technical data teams have visibility into the commercial value and cost of their projects?
real_qa.r: Technical teams cannot remain cost centers or enablers only. When they lack business context, they propose only technical solutions like buying new tools or adding storage, focusing on what they need rather than what value they return. Investors now require clear returns on investment for every organizational unit, making it impossible to justify teams without demonstrable business impact.
real_qa.requete: data teams business value visibility ROI

real_qa.q: What are the early warning signs that data and AI spending is getting out of control in organizations?
real_qa.r: Three common patterns indicate spending is out of control: data teams are highly reactive, spending more than 50% of time fixing incidents and support tickets rather than innovation; data team burnout from constantly trying to supply business needs; and the business unable to make decisions, evidenced by executives pulling CSV files in management meetings instead of trusting dashboard KPIs.
real_qa.requete: signs data spending out of control warning

real_qa.q: How should organizations approach prioritization to avoid wasting money on data projects that sound valuable but lack business impact?
real_qa.r: The value should come first, followed only by cost and execution planning. Currently, companies invest in projects because they follow industry trends, such as adopting AI initiatives without questioning actual value relative to cost. A system is needed to evaluate upfront what value will be delivered before committing resources, rather than attempting to prove ROI after shipping.
real_qa.requete: prioritize data projects business impact value first

real_qa.q: What does it mean for data teams to shift from a technical culture to a business-oriented culture focused on impact?
real_qa.r: Data teams must move away from ownership being purely technical and instead be driven by the impact they create for the business. This includes clear ownership of outcomes and requests from business units, ensuring that when a business unit like marketing requests a dashboard, they take actual ownership of value delivery rather than just building and handing off the tool, which currently causes support issues and unclear accountability.
real_qa.requete: data teams business oriented culture impact ownership
